proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, insulating lithium phosphate that is a well-known protective coating for oxide cathodes such as LiCoO2. Its phosphate chemistry is compatible with the PS4 framework of the sulfide electrolyte, and it is expected to have low interfacial reactivity with both sides at 4.0 V. It is a reasonable first test of the coating penalty.

LiF is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li salt with very high oxidative stability, so it should resist decomposition at 4.0 V against LiCoO2. Its fluoride chemistry is also relatively inert toward the thiophosphate electrolyte, which makes it a reasonable first test of a low-penalty, insulating interlayer.

Its oxide chemistry is established for LiCoO2 and sulfide interfaces, and borate coatings are reported to limit sulfide-oxide interfacial reactions. It is a chemically distinct borate family from the earlier phosphate and fluoride tests.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 (phosphate) and LiF (halide) tests set a baseline for insulating interlayers; Li3BO3 explores a different, borate family with a similar Li-rich, wide-gap, oxide-type character.
